narrative: Material PL2__MDEEA788 exhibits erratic daily demand (mean 350 units, CV 0.625) across 220 working days with 91.8% active demand days and no statistically significant trend. Lead times are highly unstable (CV 0.891, mean 1.54 days) and represent the dominant driver of safety stock requirements, with sigma_LTD of 582 units. An (r,Q) policy is recommended: a reorder point of 1,534 units and order quantity of 3,049 units (EOQ-based) achieves the 95% service level target, utilises only 52% of available storage, and requires a modest $860/year additional holding cost investment over the current zero-safety-stock SAP baseline.
warnings: SAP safety lead time of 4.5 days exceeds statistical optimum of 2.53 days — recommend reducing to avoid excess pipeline inventory
Lead time CV of 0.891 classified as unstable — safety stock is dominated by lead time variance rather than demand variance

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but frequent demand (92% active days) with unstable lead times favours a continuous-review (r,Q) model: reorder when on-hand inventory hits the reorder point r, replenish a fixed EOQ quantity Q. This avoids the overhead of periodic review while providing tight stockout protection calibrated to lead-time demand variance.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation at 52.1% (4,007 / 7,688 units) — capacity constraint does not bind. No service-level or cost penalty from the storage ceiling.
